title: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
subtitle: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with an IgM paraprotein · MYD88 L265P in ~90%+ · treat symptoms and IgM complications, not the IgM number · genotype (MYD88/CXCR4) steers BTKi vs chemoimmunotherapy
source: Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (NCCN; IWWM-2, IWWM-11 and IWWM-12 consensus panels) verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Definitions and the IgM differential
rows: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL) in the marrow + an IgM monoclonal protein of any size. IWWM-2 and IWWM-11: no IgM or marrow-% cutoff separates WM from IgM MGUS — the diagnosis rests on marrow histology + immunophenotype
IgM M-protein, no LPL on marrow, no symptoms. Progresses to lymphoma/WM at ~1.5%/yr. IWWM-11 splits it: plasma-cell type (MYD88 wild-type — myeloma/AL lineage) vs B-cell type (may be MYD88-mutant)
Meets WM criteria, no treatment indication → observe. 72% progress (median follow-up 7.8 yr). Progression risk: IgM ≥4,500 mg/dL, marrow ≥70%, β2M ≥4 mg/L, albumin ≤3.5; MYD88 wild-type HR 2.7
CD138+ plasma cells without a B-cell/LPL component, t(11;14), MYD88 wild-type, lytic lesions. Treat as myeloma — not WM
Can make IgM and show plasmacytic differentiation. MYD88 L265P absent or rare — the most useful discriminator
Symptoms from the IgM itself (neuropathy, cryo, CAD, amyloid) without overt lymphoma — still may need clone-directed therapy

blocks.heading: Workup
items: SPEP + immunofixation, quantitative IgM (SPEP M-spike and nephelometric IgM are not interchangeable — follow one method), free light chains, β2-microglobulin, albumin, LDH, CBC, CMP
Marrow biopsy: intertrabecular LPL infiltrate; surface IgM+, CD19+, CD20+, CD22+, with CD138+ plasma cells; usually CD5− CD10− CD23− (variants do not exclude WM)
Molecular on marrow before any therapy (IWWM-11): AS-PCR for MYD88 L265P and CXCR4 S338X on whole marrow; CXCR4 + TP53 sequencing and 6q/17p FISH on CD19-selected cells
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for nodes/spleen. Serum viscosity + fundoscopy if IgM is high or any HVS symptom

Targeted: cryoglobulins (draw and transport at 37°C), DAT + cold agglutinin titer, anti-MAG + EMG if neuropathy, NT-proBNP/troponin, urine protein, fat pad if amyloid suspected, MRI brain/spine + CSF if CNS symptoms
Prognosis: IPSSWM — age >65, Hb ≤11.5, plt ≤100, β2M >3 mg/L, M-protein >7 g/dL; 5-yr OS 87% / 68% / 36% (low/int/high). Not a treatment trigger

blocks.heading: IgM-mediated complications — each managed differently
rows: Blurred vision, headache, epistaxis/oronasal bleeding, dizziness, confusion, heart failure. Fundoscopy: dilated “sausage” veins, hemorrhages, papilledema. Viscosity poorly predicts symptoms per patient. Plasmapheresis first (IgM is ~80% intravascular, so it clears efficiently), then cytoreduce — pheresis alone is a bridge. Avoid RBC transfusion until pheresed

Slowly progressive, distal, symmetric sensory-predominant demyelinating neuropathy with ataxia/tremor. EMG + anti-MAG titer; joint heme-neuro care. Rituximab-based therapy; stabilization is the realistic goal. Avoid bortezomib (and vincristine)
Raynaud's, acral necrosis, purpura, vasculitic neuropathy, GN. Draw at 37°C or it is missed. Keep warm; plasmapheresis for severe; rapid cytoreduction (BR, BDR)
Chronic hemolysis with cold acrocyanosis; DAT C3d+, IgMκ titer. Keep warm, warm IV fluids/blood. Rituximab-based (BR most active); sutimlimab blocks C1s for hemolysis
Lambda light chain, cardiac/renal/nerve. Treat as AL: bortezomib- or bendamustine-based; daratumumab. cBTKi not recommended (IWWM-11)

Headache, cognitive change, cranial nerve palsies, gait. MRI brain + spine with gadolinium, CSF cytology/flow + MYD88 PCR. BTKi cross the BBB: ibrutinib (n=28: 85% symptom improvement, 2-yr EFS 80%); IWWM-12 made zanubrutinib a standard. Alternatives: HD-MTX / HD-araC, fludarabine

blocks.heading: Genotype drives BTKi choice
rows: Drives NF-κB via IRAK/BTK. Supports the diagnosis (rare in MZL, absent in myeloma). MYD88 wild-type: weaker BTKi response (ibrutinib major response 29%), worse OS — favor chemoimmunotherapy

Nonsense/frameshift C-tail mutations; higher IgM + marrow burden, more hyperviscosity. Slower, shallower BTKi responses: TN ibrutinib major response 71% vs 94%, VGPR 7% vs 31%, time to major response 7.3 vs 1.8 mo
Adverse; IWWM-11 counts TP53 and 6q/17p among essential pre-treatment tests

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — first-line evidence, relapse, response, dosing and trials

blocks.heading: First-line options — the evidence
rows: IWWM/NCCN preferred chemoimmunotherapy. Randomized evidence is StiL NHL1 (BR beat R-CHOP in indolent NHL, WM a small subgroup). Rituximab maintenance after BR: no benefit overall (StiL NHL7-MAINTAIN)

Phase 2, n=72: ORR 83% (CR 7%), 2-yr PFS 67%; grade 3–4 neutropenia only 9%. Slow: median time to response 4.1 mo. ECWM-1: adding bortezomib (B-DRC) did not improve PFS (24-mo 80.6% vs 72.8%, P=0.32) but responses came faster (3.0 vs 5.5 mo)
Weekly-bortezomib EMN regimen: ORR 85%, median PFS 42 mo; neuropathy 46% (grade ≥3 7%). Bortezomib lead-in blunts rituximab flare. Zoster prophylaxis mandatory

iNNOVATE (phase 3, n=150): IR vs placebo-R — final median PFS NR vs 20.3 mo, HR 0.25; benefit regardless of MYD88/CXCR4. Adding ibrutinib cut rituximab IgM flare (8% vs 47%). Grade ≥3 AF 12% vs 1%, HTN 13% vs 4%

ASPEN (phase 3, n=201 MYD88-mutant): primary endpoint VGPR+CR 28% vs 19%, P=0.09 — not met. Final (44 mo): VGPR+CR 36% vs 25%; CXCR4-mutant 21% vs 10%. Less AF (7.9% vs 23.5%), HTN, bleeding, diarrhea; more neutropenia. FDA-approved Aug 2021
Single-arm phase 2, n=106: ORR 93% TN and R/R; grade 3–4 AF 1%. Not FDA-approved for WM
Fixed-duration TN trial: VGPR 42% but ventricular arrhythmia 9% incl. 2 deaths → stopped early. Not a standard

blocks.heading: Fixed-duration vs continuous — how to choose
items: Chemoimmunotherapy: finite (~6 mo), then time off therapy; myelosuppression, infections; the better fit for MYD88 wild-type and a reasonable one for CXCR4-mutant disease
cBTKi: oral, rapid Hb recovery, indefinite — cost, cumulative AF/HTN/bleeding, and IgM rebound if stopped. Best in MYD88-mutant/CXCR4-WT; zanubrutinib over ibrutinib for tolerability

IgM lags the marrow: IgM can plateau or rise transiently (rituximab flare; bortezomib/rituximab-era discordance) — do not call progression on IgM alone; confirm, check marrow/Hb/nodes. BR/DRC responses deepen for months after the last cycle

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory
items: Durable first remission → the same regimen can be reused; early relapse or refractory → switch class

Ibrutinib withdrawal: IgM rebound (≥25%) in 73% of discontinuations, half within 4 weeks, some with HVS; salvage works better if started within 2 weeks. Continue the BTKi until the next therapy starts; hold only ~3–7 days peri-procedure

Pirtobrutinib (non-covalent; binds C481-mutant BTK): BRUIN WM n=80 (79% cBTKi-exposed) — ORR 82.5% (81% post-cBTKi), major response ~72%. Not FDA-approved for WM (MCL/CLL only) — single-arm, off-label
Venetoclax 200→800 mg daily ×2 yr: ORR 84%, major 81%, median PFS 30 mo; slower after BTKi (4.5 vs 1.4 mo); CXCR4 did not matter. Neutropenia 45%. Off-label

Also: bortezomib/carfilzomib-based, BR after BTKi, clinical trials (BTK degraders, CXCR4 antagonists, bispecifics). Autologous SCT for select chemosensitive young patients. Transformation to DLBCL → treat as DLBCL

blocks.heading: Response (IWWM-6 / simplified IWWM-11)
rows: Normal IgM, negative immunofixation, no marrow disease, resolved nodes/spleen
50–89% IgM reduction  ·  major response = PR or better
≥25% IgM rise from nadir (confirmed) or new disease/complication
blocks.footnote: IWWM-11 lets PR/VGPR be called on serum IgM alone, with guidance for flare/rebound. ORR in WM trials includes minor responses — compare major response rates across studies.

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1–2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² d1, q28d ×6
Dexamethasone 20 mg IV + rituximab 375 mg/m² d1 + cyclophosphamide 100 mg/m² PO BID d1–5, q21d ×6
Cycle 1 bortezomib alone 1.3 mg/m² d1,4,8,11; then 1.6 mg/m² weekly d1,8,15,22 q35d ×4; dex 40 mg + rituximab 375 in cycles 2 and 5. SC bortezomib in practice
160 mg BID or 320 mg daily, continuous
420 mg daily, continuous; iNNOVATE rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly, weeks 1–4 and 17–20
Ramp 200 → 800 mg daily, up to 2 yr; TLS precautions

blocks.heading: Monitoring and prophylaxis
items: HBsAg + anti-HBc before any anti-CD20 — entecavir if core-Ab positive. Acyclovir/valacyclovir with bortezomib (zoster in 4 of the first 7 BDR patients) and commonly with BR and BTKi

BTKi: baseline ECG and BP; ask about palpitations; treat HTN. AF → rate control, weigh anticoagulation with bleeding; switch ibrutinib → zanubrutinib. No warfarin; avoid fish oil/vit E; hold ~3–7 days around surgery. Strong CYP3A inhibitors → dose-adjust
Bortezomib: neuropathy check every cycle; weekly + SC dosing lowers it; dose-reduce at grade 2 with pain
Rituximab: IgM before each dose; hold or pre-pherese if IgM is high (commonly ≥4,000 mg/dL); a rising IgM in the first months is often flare, not progression
IgM + CBC q1–3 mo on therapy; SPEP/IgM q3–6 mo in remission. Same lab, same method

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Ibrutinib-R vs placebo-R — median PFS NR vs 20.3 mo, HR 0.25, genotype-independent
Zanubrutinib vs ibrutinib — VGPR+CR primary not met (28 vs 19%); far less AF
B-DRC vs DRC — no PFS gain; faster response
Phase 2 — ORR 85%, median PFS 42 mo, weekly bortezomib
Phase 2 — CXCR4 and MYD88 genotype set depth and speed
R/R — major response 81%, median PFS 30 mo
